status: Fixed in source; formal backlog closeout recorded 2026-09-01
area: Completion evidence copied mutable certificate diagnostics into its own terminal dependency
finding: The completion compiler treated the independent certificate as both a terminal authorization input and a source of detailed mutable diagnostics. Certificate details can legitimately change when reviewer or publication state changes, so copying them into completion evidence creates a reverse certificate-to-completion freshness edge and prevents the closeout chain from reaching a stable fixed point. This is distinct from certificate pending self-digest validation: the defect is the dependency direction, not a digest comparison.
expectedBehavior: Completion evidence consumes only the certificate's terminal authorization state: proven requires a readable, non-pending, diagnostic-free, release-authorized certificate; otherwise the affected requirement remains fail-closed with final-certificate-not-proven. Detailed certificate diagnostics remain addressable on the certificate itself and must not be mirrored into an upstream completion projection.
evidenceOrRepro: During the 0341 closeout replay, a certificate correctly reported mutable evidence-uncommitted diagnostics for its own generated inputs. scripts/compile-runbook-completion-evidence.ts appended those details to completion diagnostics, making the completion report stale whenever the certificate surface moved. The repaired observeFinalCertificate preserves final-certificate-not-proven on failure but no longer copies mutable diagnostic detail. Direct completion --mode validate then replayed successfully while retaining not-complete for the 14 genuinely unproven requirement rows.
followUp: Current runbook-completion-evidence regression verifies that a proven/authorized certificate emits no completion diagnostics, while a certificate containing volatile detail reduces only to final-certificate-not-proven. Keep certificate detail fail-closed and independently inspectable; do not mirror it upstream into completion evidence.
